title: Dedicated staged rollouts: add force-promote + hold/resume with admin guardrails
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Context: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) support promote/abort and automated gate evaluation. During beta we hit cases where (a) telemetry lag/missing metrics made gates "UNKNOWN" and blocked promotion, (b) a canary partition induced transient 429s and operators needed an immediate hold while investigating, and (c) SRE needed an explicit, auditable escape hatch for incident mitigation. This PR adds two admin-only emergency controls: (1) force-promote to advance a rollout stage while explicitly bypassing gate evaluation and (2) hold/resume to freeze a running rollout (no automatic gate polling changes and no stage transitions) until resumed or aborted.

What’s in this PR: - API: Adds POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}:force_promote and POST ...:hold (plus ...:resume) endpoints, reusing idempotency keys + optimistic concurrency from promote/abort. - RBAC: Requires new permission scope dedicated_rollouts.override (admin-only; not exposed to customer-admin). Requests must include override_reason and an optional ticket_ref (SUP/INC/INT) for traceability. - State machine: Introduces HELD as a first-class rollout state; HELD blocks promote/force_promote unless resume is called (abort allowed from HELD). Force-promote is allowed only from RUNNING and only if a next stage exists; it advances stage pointer and updates rollout state consistently with normal promotion logic. - Gate evaluation: Force-promote bypasses policy-engine gate evaluation and marks the stage transition with gate_result=OVERRIDDEN. - Audit logging: Emits explicit audit events for DEDICATED_POOL_ROLLOUT_HELD, DEDICATED_POOL_ROLLOUT_RESUMED, and DEDICATED_POOL_ROLLOUT_FORCE_PROMOTED. Payload includes actor, actor_type, pool_id, rollout_id, from_stage_id, to_stage_id, override_reason, ticket_ref, and request_id/idempotency_key. - API warnings: Adds warnings[] in action responses when an override is used (force-promote) or when a rollout is currently HELD (promote returns 409 with a warning explaining required resume). - Guardrails: Rejects force-promote when gates are currently PASS (to prevent casual bypassing), unless force=true is explicitly set (double-confirmation for admin tooling). Also rejects hold/resume without reason to improve post-incident review quality.

Operational notes: - These endpoints are behind the existing feature flag dedicated_staged_rollouts_v1, but RBAC is still enforced when enabled. - Audit events are emitted from the control plane (same path as promote/abort) to ensure export + retention behavior matches existing rollout actions.

Tests: - Added unit tests for state transitions (RUNNING->HELD->RUNNING), override validation, and RBAC enforcement. - Added integration coverage in the staged-rollouts test harness for: hold during gate evaluation, resume, and force-promote with missing metrics.

Follow-ups: - Console UI will surface HELD state + warnings (separate PR). - Audit log export pipeline needs to be updated to include the new event types (tracked in INT-1951).

Checklist: - [x] RBAC reviewed (Kaitlyn) - [x] Audit schema reviewed (SRE/Compliance) - [x] Added docs strings for admin tooling (errors + warnings) - [x] Added tests for idempotency + concurrency edge cases
commits: control-plane: add HELD state + override actions to rollout FSM
authz: enforce dedicated_rollouts.override permission + require override_reason
audit: emit held/resumed/force-promoted events with full payload
api: return warnings[] for override actions + 409 guidance when held
tests: add unit + integration scenarios for hold/resume and force-promote
review_conversation:
Jordan Lee (review): Can we be explicit about semantics when telemetry is missing? I want force-promote to be the only bypass; promote should remain fail-closed on UNKNOWN. Also, please ensure HELD prevents background promotion by any automation.

Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. Promote remains unchanged (fail-closed on UNKNOWN unless policy explicitly allows). HELD now blocks both promote and force-promote with 409 unless resumed; abort remains allowed. Gate polling continues but does not trigger any stage transitions.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (security): dedicated_rollouts.override must not be granted to customer-admin. Where is this permission assigned? Also, require a reason string (min length) and log it.

Benji Okafor (author): Permission is only in the internal admin role bundle (rbac/policies/internal_admin.json). Added validation: override_reason required, trimmed, min 10 chars; stored in audit payload and action response. No changes to customer role bundles.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please add an audit field for ticket_ref and make it easy to grep from SIEM exports. Also, can we include from/to stage ids and rollout revision for concurrency debugging?

Benji Okafor (author): Added ticket_ref optional string; included from_stage_id/to_stage_id and rollout_etag in the audit payload. Also added request_id and idempotency_key for correlation.

Ethan Park (platform): Force-promote should be hard to click. Double-confirmation looks good. But why block force-promote when gates are PASS?

Benji Okafor (author): Guardrail based on observed operator behavior in beta: it’s easy to bypass gates “just to move forward.” If gates PASS, normal promote is available and safer. If someone insists, they can set force=true which records an additional override flag in the audit event.

Chloe Martin (console backend): The warnings[] field—can you confirm it won’t break existing clients? Our console backend expects action responses to deserialize strictly.

Benji Okafor (author): We only add a new optional field (warnings) and do not change existing fields. Updated protobuf + JSON tags so unknown fields are ignored in older clients. Added a console contract test in our internal SDK harness to ensure decode succeeds.
release_notes: Admin-only emergency controls for Dedicated staged rollouts: hold/resume and force-promote (with required reason + audit logging).
Action responses now include warnings[] for override/held guidance (non-breaking additive field).
